scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Blending and splitting without reaction
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Two independently specified feeds → mixer → composition-preserving splitter.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Combine and partition material without introducing hidden chemical or equilibrium assumptions.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: Compatible material identities; independent feed states; explicit flow bases; outlet pressure rule and heat/work assumptions supplied by the unit model.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Resolve the outlet thermal state from the specified balance constraints. Distinguish a mechanical split from an equilibrium separation. Permit a property request independent of total flow.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: Preserve each nonreacting component and the declared energy balance. An ideal mechanical splitter preserves intensive state and composition while changing flow. Recombining its products reproduces the original balance state within fixture tolerances.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: Reject incompatible component mappings or enthalpy conventions rather than silently averaging temperatures or dropping components.

acceptance_tests.witness: Run two-feed mixing under declared pressure/heat rules, then a composition-preserving split and recombination. Check component flows and energy; splitting changes quantities, not the material’s intensive state.
Supply incompatible reference conventions or an invalid split; reject or require explicit boundary treatment instead of averaging temperatures or dropping components.

scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Sensible heating and heat exchange
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Single-phase liquid or gas → heater/cooler; repeat as one side of an exchanger.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Support both a specified outlet temperature with computed duty and a specified duty with computed outlet state.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: Feed state and amount flow; pressure or pressure-drop rule; one thermal specification; a compatible caloric method.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Provide enthalpy and heat capacity where required. For equipment rating, provide the requested conductivity and viscosity separately; the unit supplies geometry and heat-transfer correlations.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: Temperature-specified and duty-specified forms agree on the same selected branch. Exchanger-side duties reconcile with the external heat-loss convention. A missing rating property does not invalidate an otherwise supported duty-only calculation.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: Reject an over-specified thermal request, or identify the unsupported rating property without inventing it.

acceptance_tests.witness: For one pinned fluid, solve temperature-specified duty and duty-specified outlet modes and verify they agree on the selected branch. Add rating demands separately.
Remove a required caloric method, then an optional rating/report property. Distinguish the blocked energy calculation from a qualified omitted optional result.

scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Liquid pumping and pressure-loss calculations
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Liquid feed → pump → pipe segment → outlet.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Use liquid thermophysical properties in pressure-changing equipment without moving equipment physics into thermodynamics.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: Liquid state; flow basis; pump efficiency or work relationship; pipe geometry and hydraulic closure supplied by the unit.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Supply density, enthalpy and viscosity; supply compressibility or additional properties only when the selected unit formulation requires them. Report the actual phase policy and validity.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: The selected pump energy relation and pipe pressure-loss relation close using properties at declared evaluation locations. A phase change is detected or explicitly excluded under a declared approximation.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: Do not continue a liquid-only hydraulic calculation as though vapor formation were impossible; return a policy-appropriate diagnostic.

acceptance_tests.witness: Use declared local density, enthalpy, and viscosity in a selected pump/pipe formulation; close its work and pressure relations and assess allowed phase behavior.
Cross the liquid-only operating assumption into vapor formation; reject or explicitly qualify a separately chosen approximation rather than continuing as single liquid.

scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Gas compression, expansion and intercooling
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Gas feed → compressor/expander → intercooler → optional subsequent stage.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Support ordinary pressure-changing gas equipment and its ideal reference state.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: Feed state; outlet pressure; unit-selected efficiency/work relation; declared phase policy.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Support the pressure–entropy reference-state calculation and the actual energy-constrained outlet. Keep the ideal reference calculation distinct from the actual equipment result.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: Reference and actual states remain separately identifiable; the actual material and energy balances close; a downstream phase change is handled by the appropriate request rather than hidden in a gas label.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: A provider lacking a usable entropy method cannot claim this scenario merely because it supports temperature–pressure flashes.

acceptance_tests.witness: Resolve an ideal-reference PS state and an actual efficiency/work-constrained outlet; retain both identities and verify individual unit and intercooler energy balances.
Remove entropy support or use an invalid inverse initializer; the reference calculation is unavailable/not initialized even if TP evaluation still works.

scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Cooling and vapor–liquid separation
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Multicomponent hydrocarbon feed → cooler → equilibrium separator → vapor and liquid products.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Establish the basic multicomponent phase-split behavior used by a flowsheet.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: Feed composition and flow; separator pressure and thermal specification; permitted phases and a pinned property configuration.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Determine phase amounts and phase compositions; evaluate properties required for balances; distinguish material redistribution from chemical reaction.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: Products reconstruct the feed component totals, satisfy the specified thermal condition, and satisfy equilibrium conditions for permitted transferable components. Stability status is reported relative to the assessed candidate phase set.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: Do not report an unverified unstable or restricted-phase solution as unrestricted stable equilibrium.

acceptance_tests.witness: Resolve the cooler/separator internal state, route vapor and liquid under declared rules, and reconstruct feed component amounts and the thermal constraint.
Return a phase-restricted or unchecked solution while claiming unrestricted stability; reject that claim without confusing it with numerical nonconvergence.

scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Pressure reduction with flashing
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Pressurized feed → adiabatic valve → downstream equilibrium state.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Support energy-constrained state resolution when pressure changes and phases may appear.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: Feed material and state; outlet pressure; valve assumptions excluding shaft work and material kinetic/potential energy changes for the reference fixture.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Resolve a pressure–enthalpy outlet request with an explicit enthalpy basis and reference convention. Preserve the input accepted state during unsuccessful trials.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: Component totals and the specified enthalpy condition are satisfied. Re-evaluation at the solved state reproduces the specified enthalpy within its fixture tolerance.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: An infeasible request, unsupported specification, ambiguous branch or numerical failure must remain distinguishable.

acceptance_tests.witness: Apply the valve’s declared adiabatic/no-work pressure change, resolve PH, and check original enthalpy and component constraints before publishing outlet state or explicit pending constraints.
Inject a converged-looking result with a failed enthalpy residual, and separately a failed call; neither may overwrite the prior accepted state.

scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Conventional equilibrium-stage distillation
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Feed → multistage column with condenser and reboiler → products.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Demonstrate that thermodynamic states exist inside equipment, not only on flowsheet connections.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: Material definition; stage locations; pressure profile and column specifications owned by the unit; compatible phase and caloric methods.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Evaluate separate vapor/liquid states and equilibrium relations at each stage. Provide the same physical relationships to repeated numerical evaluation or a coupled process formulation without prescribing the global solver.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: Stage and whole-column balances close; phase relations are satisfied at accepted stages; trial states are not exposed as converged products. Removing a required property identifies the affected stage or operation.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: Local property success must not imply stage, column or flowsheet convergence.

acceptance_tests.witness: Evaluate staged vapor/liquid states in an actual column formulation; verify accepted local phase relations, stage balances, whole-column balance, and required outer convergence.
Remove a needed property at one stage or leave temporary initialization constraints active; identify the location and do not publish converged products.

scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Nonideal-liquid separation and azeotropic behavior
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Polar liquid feed → flash or equilibrium-stage separation; alcohol/water is a candidate fixture family.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Prevent a hydrocarbon-only model architecture while keeping phase behavior and caloric behavior explicitly compatible.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: Liquid nonideality method, vapor-phase convention, compatible standard states, required interaction data, and a fixture with independently characterized phase behavior.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Represent a configured vapor/liquid method combination without treating every method as the same kind of equation of state. Resolve the declared equilibrium and heat duties.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: The chosen fixture reproduces its reference phase topology and separation limitation within stated data tolerances. A converged but qualitatively wrong phase diagram does not pass.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: Missing interaction parameters, inappropriate method combinations and unsupported extrapolation remain visible; a numerical fallback must not silently replace the physical model.

acceptance_tests.witness: Use pinned nonideal phase data to verify the fixture’s required qualitative phase topology as well as quantitative tolerances and compatible energy predictions.
Remove an essential interaction parameter or force ideal fallback. The original nonideal fixture must not pass from solver convergence alone.

scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Physical absorption, humidification and gas dissolution
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Gas and liquid feeds → nonreactive contact stage → gas and liquid outlets.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Cover dissolved gases and water transfer without making every gas–liquid operation chemically reactive.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: Distinct phase compositions; declared transferable components; appropriate phase partition convention; gas reporting basis such as wet gas, dry gas or per unit dry carrier where used.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Evaluate physical partitioning and phase-specific caloric properties. Preserve phase eligibility and any nontransferring carrier assumptions.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: Transferred amounts and energy reconcile across the unit. Wet/dry reporting conversions preserve actual material quantities. No reaction occurs without a declared reaction model.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: An undefined Henry-law/reference convention or missing gas–solvent data must not be hidden as ideal partitioning.

acceptance_tests.witness: Resolve a nonreactive gas/liquid contacting fixture with declared transfer eligibility and dilute-solute conventions; reconcile actual amounts/energy and wet/dry reports.
Introduce chemical redistribution without a reaction definition or omit the solubility/reference convention; reject the altered or incomplete problem.

scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Liquid–liquid extraction and decanting
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Feed and solvent → contacting stage → decanter → two liquid products.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Require multiple instances of one phase category and phase-pair-specific behavior.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: A documented partially miscible system; compatible parameters; permitted liquid phases; temperature, pressure and material amounts.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Determine distinct liquid phase compositions and amounts. Associate an interfacial property with a particular phase pair when requested. Do not use output-array position as physical identity.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: Both liquid products have distinct meaningful identities, reconstruct the feed, and satisfy the selected equilibrium checks. Reordering provider outputs does not change physical results.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: A method unable to represent the required liquid split must be rejected or declared unsupported, not patched by duplicating one liquid phase.

acceptance_tests.witness: Resolve a supported two-liquid fixture and rerun with reordered provider candidates. Preserve physical state after valid matching and attach interfacial properties to the correct pair.
A duplicated single liquid or an ambiguous phase correspondence cannot become two unique accepted liquid products.

scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Vapor–liquid–liquid separation
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Gas/organic/aqueous feed → three-phase separator → gas and two liquid outlets.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Exercise simultaneous competing phase allocations rather than separate unrelated binary flashes.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: A documented three-phase fixture; candidate phase set; material composition and thermal/mechanical specifications.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Allocate all components over a shared equilibrium problem or a validated equivalent solution procedure. Identify absent and present phases explicitly.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: All three products reconcile material and energy. The appropriate interphase equilibrium conditions hold for the permitted transfers; phase appearance/disappearance is well defined at adjacent test points.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: A two-phase-only provider cannot claim success by ignoring an allowed aqueous or organic liquid phase.

acceptance_tests.witness: Resolve vapor plus two liquids in a shared material problem and verify component/thermal residuals, phase relations, and adjacent phase-appearance behavior.
Reject a two-phase-only replacement, or an assembly of independent flashes that double-counts material, as a solution of the original three-phase request.

scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Water and steam through saturation
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Condensate → pump → boiler → expansion or heat delivery → condenser.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Support a specialized pure-fluid configuration while exercising saturation and thermal balances.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: Pure water identity; compatible package; subcooled, saturated, two-phase and superheated fixture states; explicit phase-fraction basis.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Distinguish saturated-liquid/vapor endpoint queries, a complete two-phase state and an underdetermined request. Retain the same reference convention around the loop.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: Pressure and saturation temperature alone do not invent an intermediate phase fraction. An additional valid specification resolves it. Loop material and energy balances close.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: Ambiguous saturation inputs receive an underdetermination diagnostic, not an arbitrary phase selection presented as a unique solution.

acceptance_tests.witness: Exercise subcooled, endpoint, allocated two-phase, and superheated water states under one caloric convention; verify the selected utility loop balances.
At pure-fluid saturation, TP alone cannot select an intermediate phase fraction; additional valid specification is required for complete allocation.

scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Pure-fluid refrigeration loop
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Evaporator → compressor → condenser → expansion valve → evaporator.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Combine specialized fluid properties with the same flowsheet request semantics used elsewhere.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: Selected pure working fluid; pressure levels; thermal boundary conditions and compressor relation; consistent reference conventions.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Support evaporation/condensation, pressure–enthalpy and pressure–entropy requests, and the separate unit energy accounting.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: Every link conserves material, individual unit balances close, and loop heat/work terms reconcile. No provider-specific fluid name becomes the authoritative material identity.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: A supported pure-fluid loop must not be advertised as support for arbitrary mixtures of that fluid.

acceptance_tests.witness: Run a pinned pure-fluid evaporator/compressor/condenser/valve loop and verify every unit balance and the loop heat/work balance under declared branch policy.
Do not generalize this success to arbitrary mixtures or conceal a failed recycle behind individually completed unit states.

scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Mixed-refrigerant phase change
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Specified refrigerant blend → evaporating/condensing loop or exchanger section.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Prevent pure-fluid quality or saturation assumptions from defining all mixture behavior.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: Blend composition, actual component identities or explicitly declared pseudo-pure approximation, candidate phases, and mixture-capable data.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Represent different liquid and vapor compositions and distinct saturation endpoints where the selected fixture requires them. Distinguish mole-based from mass-based phase fraction.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: The mixture fixture preserves composition through the loop and matches reference endpoint/temperature-glide behavior within its validation scope. A pseudo-pure approximation is identified as a separate configuration.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: Do not interpret a mixture as a pure fluid merely to obtain a convenient flash call.

acceptance_tests.witness: For a true mixture fixture, preserve overall composition while resolving distinct phase compositions and the documented endpoint/glide behavior.
A pseudo-pure approximation or a changed mass/mole quality basis is a different configuration, not an unnoticed shortcut to the original result.

scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Assay-derived petroleum pseudocomponents
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Assay or boiling-curve description → characterization → blend/heating/separation flowsheet.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Treat characterized materials as reproducible model inputs rather than unidentified chemicals.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: Original assay, stated test/basis conventions, cut definitions, characterization methods, estimated properties and provenance.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Create a reproducible component representation and use it in selected thermal/separation calculations. Retain the link to the originating assay and all estimation assumptions.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: The characterization reconciles the declared assay quantities within agreed tolerances. Saving/reloading preserves the cut definitions and property values. Changing characterization creates a distinguishable configuration and invalidates dependent results.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: Do not invent a registry identity, atom balance or exact molecular structure for a cut; do not claim support for an uncharacterized assay.

acceptance_tests.witness: Characterize a pinned assay into declared cuts, reconcile its quantities, perform supported thermal/separation use, and save/reconstruct the assay and generated property definitions.
A PVT-only pseudo route cannot pass heating/PH coverage; missing molecular structure does not authorize invented exact atom/registry identities.

scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Black-oil or other reduced petroleum representation
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Bulk oil/gas/water description → pressure/temperature changes → supported surface-separation calculation.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Permit a useful engineering representation without falsely promising molecular-resolution equilibrium.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: Model-specific bulk quantities; standard-condition conventions; empirical correlations; declared supported outputs and operating envelope.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Keep this representation distinct from an assay-characterized compositional mixture. Expose only calculations justified by its data and correlations.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: Reported standard/actual quantities and phase partitions follow the selected empirical model. Unsupported chemical potentials or detailed-species requests remain unsupported.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: No silent conversion from bulk oil characterization to an invented detailed molecular composition.

acceptance_tests.witness: Run a pinned reduced petroleum model using its actual/standard-condition conventions and explicitly limited partition/property operations.
Detailed molecular chemical potentials or a unique detailed composition remain unsupported unless additional justified characterization and mapping are supplied.

scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Specified-conversion reaction
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Reactant feeds → conversion reactor → cooling/separation.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Separate process-imposed reaction extent from equilibrium prediction.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: Stoichiometry, selected conversion or extent, phase participation, feed composition and an explicit heat-accounting convention.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Calculate resulting amounts and thermal requirements under the unit-imposed reaction extent. Treat conversion as an input assumption, not a computed equilibrium state.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: Elemental and total mass balances close when defined; stoichiometric consumption is feasible; reaction heat is included exactly once under the chosen energy formulation. Total molecular moles are not incorrectly required to be conserved.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: Reject impossible conversion or unbalanced specified chemistry rather than clipping negative product quantities.

acceptance_tests.witness: Apply a feasible fixed conversion with explicit reaction sequence and thermal mode; verify stoichiometry, mass/elements where defined, and exactly-once reaction energy.
An infeasible fixed conversion must fail. A separately authorized reactant-limited alternative is qualified and cannot pass the original strict fixture.

scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Chemical-equilibrium reaction
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Specified reactant mixture → isothermal or energy-constrained equilibrium reactor → outlet.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Support changes in chemical species in addition to redistribution among phases.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: Admissible species, conserved quantities, reaction-equilibrium or chemical-potential formulation, phase policy, and thermal constraints.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Resolve equilibrium under declared closed/open-system conditions. Keep phase equilibrium, chemical equilibrium and reaction inhibition separately identifiable.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: Conserved elements and charge, where applicable, reconcile; admissible equilibrium conditions hold; the thermal constraint is satisfied. Restricting the species or phase set changes the declared problem rather than silently changing the solver.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: A vapor–liquid flash with fixed chemical species totals is not accepted as chemical-equilibrium capability.

acceptance_tests.witness: Run a pinned isothermal or energy-constrained chemical-equilibrium fixture; verify species/phase restrictions, relevant conserved totals, and thermal conditions.
A fixed-species VLE result is not chemical equilibrium; undisclosed external exchange or expanded species scope fails the original problem.

scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Kinetically controlled reaction
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Feed → stirred or distributed reactor → outlet.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Allow finite-rate chemistry to consume thermophysical properties without the property service imposing equilibrium.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: Rate law, basis and units, participating phases, material state, and unit-owned residence time/geometry/transport assumptions.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Supply activities, concentrations or other declared rate-law inputs, as well as compatible thermal properties. Evaluate local states at required internal locations.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: Rate and property conventions agree; the accepted reactor solution closes the relevant balances. Changing residence time changes the unit solution without changing the identity of the property package.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: Do not replace a finite-rate reaction by equilibrium because that is the only supported backend operation.

acceptance_tests.witness: Use matched rate/property bases in a selected reactor formulation, evaluate required internal states, and close accepted balances as residence time changes.
A finite-rate request cannot be replaced with equilibrium, and an unqualified concentration conversion cannot feed the rate expression.

scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Reactive separation
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Reacting liquid/vapor system → reactive contacting or equilibrium-stage separation → products.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Test that chemical and phase transformations can coexist in one local material description.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: A documented compatible reacting-mixture fixture; declared reaction mode, stage assumptions, phase-transfer eligibility and energy conventions.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Represent simultaneous or explicitly approximated reaction/phase-equilibrium coupling. Keep the closure choice visible and compatible with the unit formulation.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: Local and overall balances and the selected reaction/phase conditions hold together. Separate standalone successes are insufficient when their coupled result violates either set of conditions.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: Do not silently sequence incompatible chemistry and flash models and label the result fully coupled equilibrium.

acceptance_tests.witness: Run one compatible reactive stage/separation formulation and jointly verify phase, chemistry, energy, and stage/whole-unit conditions.
Separate chemistry and flash successes that do not satisfy the coupled constraints do not establish reactive-separation success.

scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Electrolyte mixing and neutralization
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Acid/base/salt feeds → mixer or neutralizer → aqueous outlet.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Support reporting composition and internal species composition as different legitimate representations.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: Apparent feed description, true species definition, charge and elemental information, thermodynamic data and reference conventions.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Resolve speciation under the declared constraints; expose reporting quantities without summing apparent and true species as separate physical inventories.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: Conserved quantities and electroneutrality, where imposed, hold. Apparent/true conversions do not double count mass. Reported pH and other quantities retain their activity/convention definitions.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: Inconsistent charge or incomplete reaction/species data produces a specific diagnostic rather than an unexplained normalization.

acceptance_tests.witness: Map an apparent electrolyte feed to true species, resolve the selected neutralization/speciation problem, and report pH/activity conventions without duplicate material.
Charge inconsistency, double-counted apparent/true species, or unsupported caloric completion prevents the affected claimed result.

scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Reactive gas absorption into aqueous liquid
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Gas feed plus aqueous solvent → absorber → gas and loaded-liquid products.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Combine gas transfer, dissolved-species chemistry and heat effects in a flowsheet context.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: Gas and aqueous definitions, speciation/reaction rules, transfer conventions, thermal properties and a chosen equilibrium-stage or rate-based unit closure.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Account for gas entering or leaving the liquid and for changes in dissolved species. Keep gas reservoirs or added titrants explicit when constrained chemistry requires them.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: Element and energy transfers reconcile across gas and aqueous descriptions. Any imposed pH/fugacity condition that requires external material exchange reports that exchange.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: A speciation-only result with no defensible caloric method does not qualify as an energy-balanced absorber calculation.

acceptance_tests.witness: Combine gas transfer and aqueous reaction under a selected contacting formulation, account for every declared gas/titrant exchange, and close energy across representations.
A speciation-only result cannot pass an energy-balanced absorber fixture; no hidden gas reservoir or implicit titrant is allowed.

scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Inert solids carried with fluid
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Liquid/gas plus inert solids → heating/transport → mechanical separation.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Represent a solid-bearing material without forcing the solids into a chemical-equilibrium calculation.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: Solid identities or empirical material descriptors, amounts, phase-specific caloric/density data, participation policy and optional particle attributes.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Carry the solids through balances; include their thermal contribution when required; distinguish mechanical separation from precipitation. Let equipment models own settling/filtering closures.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: Solid and fluid quantities reconcile. Equilibrium-inactive solids do not disappear. A mixture viscosity or other effective property is returned only under a declared bulk closure.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: Do not assign a fictitious vapor pressure or molar basis to an empirical solid merely to fit a fluid API.

acceptance_tests.witness: Carry equilibrium-inactive solid material through fluid heating and mechanical separation, including its justified caloric contribution and any declared bulk closure.
An inert solid cannot disappear into an equilibrium routine or be assigned fictitious vapor pressure/molar identity to fit its API.

scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Crystallization and precipitation
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Solution → cooling/evaporation or reagent addition → crystal-bearing material → separation.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Distinguish equilibrium solid formation from inert-solid transport and from crystal growth kinetics.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: Dissolved species/components, admissible solid identities, compatible solution/solid data, thermal constraints and phase policy.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Determine equilibrium solid quantities or report the selected constrained calculation. Keep particle-size distribution and nucleation/growth modeling external unless explicitly added.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: Conserved quantities reconcile; present phases satisfy the relevant equilibrium tests; absent allowed phases satisfy the declared stability/saturation checks or are marked unchecked. Thermal quantities include the selected phase-change/chemical convention once.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: Do not treat a saturation calculation alone as a prediction of crystal size or kinetic yield.

acceptance_tests.witness: Resolve a bounded compatible precipitation fixture with named solid forms, quantify present solids, check conserved totals and thermal targets, and assess absent candidates as declared.
A saturation index is not crystal size or kinetic yield; unsupported multicomponent solid capability remains a specific rejection.

scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Gas–solid chemical transformation
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Gas and reactive solid → contactor/reactor → gas and solid products.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Ensure reactive solids are not represented as inert carrier mass or dissolved fluid by default.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: Solid reactant/product identities, gas species, reaction mode, compatible solid/gas caloric data and unit-owned contact/transport assumptions.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Evaluate the requested reaction-equilibrium or kinetic property relationships for the declared phases. Permit unreacted and product solids to coexist as distinct entities.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: Conserved quantities and energy reconcile across gas and solids. The calculation distinguishes equilibrium restrictions from finite-rate limits.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: Unsupported solid-solution or polymorph behavior remains explicit rather than being approximated as an ideal liquid without authorization.

acceptance_tests.witness: Run a bounded gas–solid reaction formulation with distinct reactant/product solids, required thermal data, and explicit equilibrium or kinetic limits.
Unsupported polymorph/solid-solution behavior cannot silently become an ideal-liquid approximation or inert carrier.

scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Rate-based nonequilibrium contacting
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Gas/liquid feeds → spatially resolved contactor → separate outlets.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Support phase-specific bulk states and local interface relationships without automatically equilibrating the entire unit.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: Separate phase temperatures and compositions where the chosen unit requires them; pressure/mechanical convention; transfer and interface assumptions.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Evaluate each bulk phase independently, plus interfacial equilibrium or driving-force properties as requested. The unit supplies interfacial area and transfer coefficients or correlations.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: A nonequilibrium bulk input remains nonequilibrium unless the unit explicitly imposes a closure. Interphase mass/energy fluxes reconcile across the unit. Required diffusivity and interfacial properties are capability-checked.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: An equilibrium flash is not substituted for a rate-based contactor or used to overwrite its phase states.

acceptance_tests.witness: Keep distinct bulk-phase states and required interface relations within a selected rate-based unit; verify transfer/energy reconciliation and property coverage.
An automatic bulk reflash or efficiency-corrected equilibrium-stage model does not pass the full specified SC-26 formulation.

scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Adsorption and membrane state extensions
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Bulk feed → adsorber or membrane contacting location → separate material domains.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Reserve a concrete extension path for surface-bound material and selective transfer.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: Bulk material states; optional adsorbed/surface inventory, loading basis and site definition; membrane-side identities and applicable chemical-potential conventions.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Represent relevant bulk and nonbulk states without labeling every surface inventory as an ordinary liquid phase. Keep isotherms, permeation laws and equipment transport relationships explicitly assigned.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: A conceptual walkthrough preserves material between bulk, permeate/retentate and optional surface storage. Unsupported surface or electrochemical requests are expressible and explicitly rejected.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: A generic untyped metadata attachment is insufficient evidence that this scenario is representable.

acceptance_tests.witness: Walk through bulk, surface storage, and selective-transfer domains with stated loading/site/basis conventions and a conserved-material transfer.
A label or arbitrary metadata field with no state, transfer, and conservation meaning fails representability; numerical support remains unclaimed.

scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Heat exchange between different property packages
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Process-fluid circuit ↔ heat exchanger ↔ independent water/refrigerant circuit.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Allow different thermodynamic configurations in one flowsheet without implying material translation.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: Independent material definitions and packages per circuit; separate reference conventions; declared heat-loss/work conventions.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Compute each circuit’s enthalpy changes independently and couple them through heat transfer. Do not require common component sets or equal numerical enthalpy zeroes.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: Energy transferred from one side reconciles with energy received by the other and any stated losses. Components never cross the wall in this scenario.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: Do not invoke a chemical component translator merely because two connected equipment sides use different packages.

acceptance_tests.witness: Couple two independent material packages through a heat exchanger, preserving within-side energy differences and no species transfer across the wall.
Differing absolute reference zeroes cannot by themselves trigger material translation; a required caloric failure cannot be hidden as optional.

scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Material transfer across a property-package boundary
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Material stream described by package A → explicit boundary treatment → region using package B.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Handle different models for the same physical material without a hidden energy or identity discontinuity.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: Common or mapped material identities; both package conventions; chosen quantities to preserve; known reference offsets and explicit discrepancy policy.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Separate a pure reference-state conversion from disagreement between physical models. Define which state is recomputed and under which constraints.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: Conserved quantities and selected boundary constraints hold. Holding temperature and pressure reports any residual enthalpy-model mismatch; holding pressure and corrected enthalpy may require a recomputed temperature. No unexplained heat source closes the gap.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: Do not promise simultaneous preservation of incompatible temperature, pressure, composition and enthalpy predictions from different models.

acceptance_tests.witness: Test a declared T/P-preserving boundary and a pressure/corrected-enthalpy-preserving boundary separately; report reference corrections and residual model disagreement.
Do not simultaneously enforce incompatible T,P,composition,H by hidden heat or by relabeling model discrepancy as a constant reference offset.

scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Translation between material representations
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Detailed/apparent material description → explicit representation map → lumped/true-species description.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Permit heterogeneous modeling fidelity while making information loss and conserved quantities explicit.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: Source and target representations; mapping rules; feasible conserved quantities; assumptions needed for any reverse reconstruction.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Translate without treating an irreversible aggregation as a bijection. Preserve provenance and distinguish reporting conversion from physical re-equilibration.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: The selected mass/element/charge or defined empirical balances reconcile. Round-trip equality is required only for reversible mappings; information lost by lumping is documented.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: Missing information for unlumping is not synthesized as a unique composition.

acceptance_tests.witness: Translate a reversible identity/order case and an irreversible aggregation case; verify the appropriate balances and document information lost.
An irreversible aggregation has no unique inverse without extra declared information; apparent-to-true mapping cannot double-count material.

scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Mass-based empirical and nonconventional materials
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Assay-described biomass, sludge, polymer granules or other engineering material → heating/mixing/separation.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Support useful limited-property process models without pretending every material is a known molecular mixture.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: Declared mass basis; empirical density/heat-capacity/enthalpy relationships as available; composition or assay descriptors and their validity.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Answer only supported requests. Permit mass/energy calculations where justified; require additional characterization before molar, elemental or chemical-potential calculations.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: A reference heat/mass-balance case runs without an invented molecular weight. A request requiring missing molecular information fails specifically. Optional empirical mixture rules are explicit.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: Do not use arbitrary molecular weight, critical constants or zero-valued missing properties to satisfy a universal fluid contract.

acceptance_tests.witness: Complete a mass/energy fixture using only justified empirical properties, with no assumed molecular weight; show its restricted property readiness.
Reject an unsupported molecular or elemental request specifically while keeping its supported empirical heating calculation usable.

scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Polymer distributions and material attributes
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Polymer/solvent feed → mixing/devolatilization location → material with retained distribution descriptors.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Reserve support for materials whose characterization is not exhausted by one molecular identity and mole fraction.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: A documented distribution or moment representation; basis; polymer/solvent descriptors; model-specific parameters and permitted reductions.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Associate distributions and derived averages with their material definition. Distinguish repeat units, molecules, segments and mass bases when relevant.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: A conceptual state-and-transfer walkthrough preserves the declared distribution information or records an explicit reduction. Unsupported detailed rheology or polymer equilibrium is not implied.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: A single arbitrary mean molecular weight is not accepted as a lossless representation of an entire distribution.

acceptance_tests.witness: Walk through transfer/mixing of a declared polymer distribution or moment description, preserving or explicitly reducing its attributes and material basis.
A single average molecular weight cannot be claimed to preserve a full distribution, and numerical detailed rheology/equilibrium remains unclaimed.

scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Inventory-based state and dynamic compatibility
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Vessel inventory at an identified time/location → material-state evaluation under volume/energy constraints.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Keep future dynamics possible without including a time integrator in the present thermodynamics scope.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: Component/species inventories or another declared material amount basis; total internal energy and total volume, or another admissible independent specification.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Represent inventory separately from flow. Permit a state request based on total quantities with the required amount information; the process model owns accumulation balances, temporal evolution and events.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: A nonempty inventory does not require a fictitious flow. Total versus specific quantities are unambiguous. A zero inventory has an explicit policy rather than undefined intensive values disguised as a physical state.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: Do not infer density from total volume alone without material amount or assume a steady-flow enthalpy request is always sufficient.

acceptance_tests.witness: Walk through a nonempty inventory state with material amounts and total U,V, and an empty-inventory variant with explicit undefined/retained intensive semantics.
Do not require a fictitious flow or infer density/unique state from total volume and energy without adequate material information.

scenario_acceptance_contracts.title: Restricted-equilibrium and metastable-state requests
scenario_acceptance_contracts.trigger: Process location with an explicit phase or reaction restriction → constrained property/state evaluation.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.objective: Separate user-imposed physical approximations from solver heuristics and global-equilibrium claims.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.inputs_and_preconditions: Named excluded phases/reactions or requested branch; rationale; validity restrictions; expected diagnostics.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.required_behavior: Represent frozen chemistry, suppressed solids or a metastable branch where a provider supports it. Keep this distinct from an initial guess and from equilibrium over all allowed candidates.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.baseline_acceptance: The result retains its restriction label and cannot be reported as unrestricted equilibrium. Removing a restriction invalidates the prior result for the changed problem.
scenario_acceptance_contracts.failure_behavior: A fallback that disables a phase or reaction without changing the declared problem is forbidden.

acceptance_tests.witness: Walk through frozen chemistry, suppressed solids, or a supported metastable branch as differently qualified requests with their restrictions retained.
Removing a restriction invalidates the old result for the new request; altered-phase retry cannot acquire unrestricted equilibrium status.

integrated_journeys.journey: Gas mixing → compression → cooling → separation → pressure reduction, with an explicit recycle.
integrated_journeys.acceptance: Verify unit material/energy balances, reference-versus-actual compressor states, PH targets, phase allocation, and recycle convergence under one captured model revision.
integrated_journeys.failure: Exhaust the recycle after successful local flashes: retain inspectable iterates but do not accept the whole-flowsheet result.

integrated_journeys.journey: A chemically justified polar separation/column case plus extraction/decanter and solvent recycle; test the full nonequilibrium variant separately.
integrated_journeys.acceptance: Verify local-state independence, nonideal phase behavior, multiple-liquid mapping, stage/whole-unit balances, and declared contacting formulation.
integrated_journeys.failure: A fixture not physically supporting all sections cannot demonstrate them by juxtaposition; an efficiency model cannot certify SC-26.

integrated_journeys.journey: Water/steam or refrigerant utility coupled through heat to a different process material; use separate justified fluid variants where required.
integrated_journeys.acceptance: Verify within-side caloric consistency, quality semantics, inverse state operations, no species exchange across the wall, and utility-loop closure.
integrated_journeys.failure: Change one side’s legitimate constant energy reference and require invariant physical heat/work; isolate optional bounding-property failures.

integrated_journeys.journey: Reaction, cooling, phase separation, and recycle using separately declared conversion, equilibrium, kinetic, and reactive-separation variants.
integrated_journeys.acceptance: Verify that each variant retains its own species authority, reaction-energy convention, required coupled conditions, and outer convergence.
integrated_journeys.failure: An impossible fixed conversion must not be converted to a limited or equilibrium solution without a new authorized problem.

integrated_journeys.journey: Aqueous preparation → reactive gas contact → precipitation → solids separation.
integrated_journeys.acceptance: Track true/apparent species, external exchanges, energy, inert versus precipitating solids, and qualified contacting formulation across all boundaries.
integrated_journeys.failure: Remove an essential caloric or transfer property: speciation may remain useful but the complete energy/rate-based process claim must fail.

integrated_journeys.journey: Assay characterization → compositional processing, with a separately declared reduced-model/package-boundary test.
integrated_journeys.acceptance: Reconstruct original assay/cuts and complete required caloric data; verify translation constraints and report irreversible aggregation/model discrepancy.
integrated_journeys.failure: PVT-only pseudocomponents or an invented inverse lumping map cannot satisfy the thermal/detailed-composition fixtures.

integrated_journeys.journey: Empirical solid-bearing material → heating → mechanical separation, with a separately qualified reactive-solid variant.
integrated_journeys.acceptance: Execute justified mass/energy operations without fictitious molecular properties; require additional explicit chemistry before the reactive extension.
integrated_journeys.failure: Request elemental balance/fugacity from a mass-only material: reject only the unsupported claim and retain supported thermal use.

integrated_journeys.journey: Conceptual surface, distribution, inventory, and restricted-state walkthroughs, each followed by a transfer/change/result operation.
integrated_journeys.acceptance: Show meaningful representation, quantity/basis and conservation semantics, permitted actions, and qualified unavailable numerical operations.
integrated_journeys.failure: Untyped metadata or a fictitious flow/unique distribution inverse cannot satisfy representability; no numerical P3 pass is implied.

synthetic_contract_fixtures.setup: A and B are synthetic mass constituents. Initial flows are A=2 kg/s, B=3 kg/s. No thermodynamic model is needed.
synthetic_contract_fixtures.stimulus: Patch A to 4 kg/s under preserve-unmentioned-component-flows; separately request total=5 kg/s while holding B=3 and A=4.
synthetic_contract_fixtures.oracle: First operation: total=7 kg/s, mass fractions A=4/7 and B=3/7. Second operation: inconsistent constraints, no accepted change.

synthetic_contract_fixtures.setup: A mock phase reports density=1000 kg/m3; enthalpy is unavailable, not zero. An unrelated accepted result already exists.
synthetic_contract_fixtures.stimulus: Request density only, then a primary enthalpy calculation, then an optional viscosity report.
synthetic_contract_fixtures.oracle: Density can succeed; primary enthalpy fails specifically; optional viscosity omission does not erase prior accepted primary results.

synthetic_contract_fixtures.setup: Deliberately synthetic constant-cp packages: h_A=T−300 and h_B=1.2(T−300)+100, in kJ/kg with T in K. The known pure reference offset from B is 100 kJ/kg. Pressure and composition are fixed.
synthetic_contract_fixtures.stimulus: At T=350 K, translate by preserving T,P; separately preserve P and reference-corrected h=50 kJ/kg.
synthetic_contract_fixtures.oracle: At equal T: h_A=50, h_B=160, corrected h_B=60, residual model discrepancy=10 kJ/kg. At corrected h=50: T_B=341.6666666667 K. There is no hidden heat source and the two boundary policies are not equivalent.

synthetic_contract_fixtures.setup: An empirical material has mass flow 2 kg/s and h=2(T−300) kJ/kg, with no molecular weight or elemental description.
synthetic_contract_fixtures.stimulus: Heat it from 300 K to 325 K with no other work/loss; then request molar enthalpy and fugacity.
synthetic_contract_fixtures.oracle: Thermal fixture duty=100 kW. Molecular requests fail specifically; no fictional molecular weight is supplied. This is a contract oracle, not a claim about any real material.

synthetic_contract_fixtures.purpose: Converged-looking inverse result with failed target
synthetic_contract_fixtures.setup: A mock PH provider returns a success flag and a candidate whose recomputed h=20 kJ/kg; the requested target is 50 kJ/kg. The acceptance tolerance is 1e−6 kJ/kg for this synthetic case.
synthetic_contract_fixtures.stimulus: Submit the candidate for state acceptance.
synthetic_contract_fixtures.oracle: Absolute enthalpy residual=30 kJ/kg, therefore CHECK_FAILED. The prior accepted result is unchanged.

synthetic_contract_fixtures.setup: Synthetic equal-formula A and B use A→B with initial amounts A=1 mol and B=0 mol; the example is only a stoichiometric contract test.
synthetic_contract_fixtures.stimulus: First request extent 0.4 mol, then strict extent 1.2 mol.
synthetic_contract_fixtures.oracle: Feasible result: A=0.6 mol, B=0.4 mol. Strict 1.2 mol is infeasible. A reactant-limited alternative, if separately authorized, cannot pass the original fixed-extent request.

synthetic_contract_fixtures.setup: A synthetic result has L-a=1 mol with x=(0.8,0.2), L-b=3 mol with x=(0.1,0.9), and one zero-amount vapor placeholder. This is not an equilibrium benchmark.
synthetic_contract_fixtures.stimulus: Reverse the provider phase order and remap by declared identity; calculate total component amounts.
synthetic_contract_fixtures.oracle: Total material=4 mol; component totals=(1.1,2.9) mol; two present liquids, zero present vapor. No extra physical phase arises from an aggregate or placeholder.

synthetic_contract_fixtures.setup: A mock request captures model revision A and an accepted result exists. The model changes to B before A completes; a second variant cancels the request before completion.
synthetic_contract_fixtures.oracle: Keep A’s candidate historical/stale or rejected, not current under B. For cancellation, do not auto-publish the late candidate. Preserve prior accepted lineage.

decisions.decision: B1 remains the scope authority. All 34 scenarios, 24 cross-cutting behaviors, and P1/P2/P3 assignments are retained. New wording refines behavior; no backend is selected.

H requirements govern the host’s behavior wherever applicable; C requirements govern claimed numerical/formulation capabilities. P1/P2 still require selected end-to-end execution and validation eventually. Unsupported per-provider results do not satisfy P1/P2 program-wide delivery.

B1 SC-17 wins over DWSIM’s observed limiting behavior. Reject an infeasible strict conversion. A separately authorized limited-conversion alternative is recorded as a different problem and cannot pass the strict fixture.

Same-model numerical retries are permitted under policy. Any changed phase/species scope, ideal substitution, or omitted equilibrium must remain an alternate problem with explicit authorization and distinct result qualification.
The qualification chain is request-specific. PVT support, caloric completion, transport support, derivatives, algorithm coverage, and initialization are not synonyms.
A default can initialize a workspace or be accepted as a named model choice; it cannot silently become a user specification. Complete replacement, patching, and rescaling have different effects.

Known extrapolation or estimated data can remain usable under authorized engineering policy. Such use is not automatically within validated scope. Numerical acceptance is not independent physical validation.
A property call, equilibrium result, unit outlet specification, accepted local state, and accepted flowsheet state carry different authority and completion claims.
Logical owners identify accountability, not services/classes. Coherent external packages, scoped mutable sessions, and equation contributions all remain admissible.
Only concrete state/action/conservation walkthroughs satisfy P3 representability. The four R3 records do not make numerical surface/polymer/UV/metastable implementations mandatory in P1/P2.
Real-fluid numerical fixtures require independently specified absolute/relative tolerances, scales, data and model conventions before execution. No universal accuracy percentage is invented.
B2/B3 source observations motivate requirements but do not make them capabilities of this simulator. This stage performs catalog consistency checks only, not thermodynamic execution or validation.

outcome_vocabulary.meaning: A constituent or provider identifier cannot be resolved uniquely.
Values, bases, or jointly imposed constraints are invalid or conflicting.
A complete-state request lacks independent information, adds unresolved extra constraints, or has not been assessed. Intentionally partial model states are not errors by themselves.
The requested changes conflict with caller-owned intensives, phase allocations, or species quantities.
The exact adapter/profile rejects the operation, or its support has not been established.
Required engine, binding, parameter data, or separately required resource is unavailable.
The selected method or energy/standard-state combination cannot be coherently applied.
The request violates its selected data/model/extrapolation policy; record numerical bounds separately.
The provider needs an admissible start or preparation failed. This is not a proof of physical infeasibility.
The constraints are demonstrated incompatible, or feasibility has not been established. Do not infer infeasibility from generic failure.
A unique branch or cross-run phase match is not justified.
Required numerical convergence was not achieved under the stated policy.
A mandatory physical postcondition fails or lacks required evidence despite any solver success flag.
An external failure with known or unknown native cause; identify affected stage/session.
The caller cancelled or the captured input/configuration revision is no longer current.
An optional property failed; primary operation status must be assessed independently.
